governed_construct: A weather-data request: an HTTP call (fetch, axios, or similar) whose URL resolves to a weather data provider, or a call through a weather-provider SDK client (e.g. the openmeteo package, openweather-api-node).
interpretation: The rule requires weather data to come from Open-Meteo. Each weather-data request in the file is one instance; it conforms when the request URL resolves to an open-meteo.com host (api.open-meteo.com, geocoding-api.open-meteo.com, etc.) or goes through the official openmeteo SDK, and it violates when it targets another weather provider (OpenWeatherMap, WeatherAPI.com, Tomorrow.io, Weatherbit, ...) directly or via that provider's SDK. Under all-instances semantics a file that uses Open-Meteo for one request and another provider for another is VIOLATED. Files with no weather-data request (including HTTP calls to unrelated APIs) are NOT_APPLICABLE. A provider URL that appears in the file but never flows into a request (log messages, blocklists) is not an instance; deciding this requires following bindings from the request call back to the URL value, which is why the rule is T3 rather than a string-literal match.
